notes: CT40's construct is a C construct: a store of an owned pointer into an object that outlives the call. No QCore syntax expresses it, so the case's artifact is the C twin in case.c, analyzed through the real unrestricted-C gateway. The scenario expects `Not certified; unsupported lifetime/publication protocol`, and that is what the gateway reports since card CTWIN-PUBLISH: the publication is refused, so the projection is withdrawn rather than completed. Two invariance controls bound what the mapping claims. `plain_pointer.c` removes `_Atomic` and does not move one byte of the verdict — the projection derives no atomicity or synchronization fact, so it cannot — and `no_release.c` removes the release instead and is still refused, so the refusal is the publication and not the `prematurely freed` half of the scenario title. Nothing here decides what reads the published object; the measurement is that no certificate is issued for a publication protocol this projection does not model.
